groups.text: It is currently 21 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

The Perplexity Portable Computer is now available for Windows users and runs on NVIDIA RTX hardware. This release marks a shift toward local processing, allowing AI agents to manage more complex tasks directly on a personal computer. By moving these operations off the cloud, the system can keep sensitive information stored securely on the device itself. This transition comes as local models become increasingly capable of handling workloads that previously required remote servers. The integration of NVIDIA RTX power enables this portable version of Perplexity to function as a local tool for users who prioritize data privacy and speed.

The United States Supreme Court has rejected Donald Trump’s bid to restrict voting by mail ahead of the November midterm elections. The ruling from the conservative supermajority court allows states to continue sending out mail ballots as they have for years, halting possible last-minute legal actions. This is a setback for the president, who has repeatedly cited debunked claims of widespread fraud to cast doubt on the security of mail-in voting, despite having voted by mail himself in 2024. Meanwhile, in Ukraine, parliament has dismissed Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko. The vote passed without a single opposing ballot, coming just one day after Kravchenko approved charges against the head of the country's anti-corruption bureau. This dismissal follows an investigation into an alleged criminal group within the Prosecutor General's Office that reportedly helped launder millions of hryvnias and protected scam call centers.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Selenskyj is performing a diplomatic balancing act following a bold announcement from U.S. President Donald Trump. While Trump claimed an agreement was reached to stop mutual attacks on energy infrastructure, Selenskyj has avoided a direct denial, instead calling it a convincing proposal. He maintains that Kyiv will support de-escalation only if Washington can ensure Moscow shows a genuine and long-term will to end the war. In other news, the rapid adoption of AI in corporate settings is forcing organizations to scramble for security guardrails, leading to a virtual event on October 8th focused on building secure enterprise AI strategies. This urgency contrasts with the slower pace of academic research; on Reddit, one machine learning researcher is questioning if a basic algorithm that solves only one of two intended problems is sufficient for a workshop submission.

The BRICS bloc is balancing urgent environmental goals against the practical needs of emerging economies. In the New Delhi Declaration adopted on September 12, twenty-one member and partner countries called for climate resilience and a reduction in greenhouse gas emissions. However, the document explicitly recognizes the role of fossil fuels in the global energy mix as a foundation for national security and economic development. To bridge this gap, the group is pursuing practical cooperation on carbon markets, hydrogen, and smart grids while upholding the Paris Agreement. In separate news from the tech world, the macOS package manager Homebrew has released version 7.0, introducing its first official graphical user interface built with SwiftUI. This new app allows users to manage packages without relying solely on the command line, though it is restricted to macOS 26 and 27. As a result, Intel-based Macs are falling into obsolescence.

OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic are calling for a coordinated slowdown in the development of frontier AI, citing urgent safety risks. To achieve this, they are seeking antitrust exemptions that would allow these dominant labs to set shared industry standards. However, critics argue the move is less about safety and more about market control. Cohere CEO Aidan Gomez has described the initiative as a cartel by another name, claiming it is an attempt to create barriers to entry and lock out competitors while weakening open-weight AI. This divide extends into politics. President Donald Trump has dismissed warnings of an AI takeover as a hoax, whereas Democrats including Barack Obama and Kamala Harris support a slowdown and increased transparency. While figures like Sam Altman and Elon Musk agree with the proposal, the push for antitrust exemptions remains a central point of contention between the industry's largest players and its smaller rivals.

Beijing has implemented sweeping travel restrictions on its citizens to protect what it calls industrial and technological security. These new exit-and-entry rules specifically target individuals deemed to have violated regulations regarding the import and export of technology, with a particular focus on artificial intelligence. The State Council says these measures safeguard national sovereignty and development interests. This includes the power to prohibit citizens from leaving China for six months to three years if they are found to have committed criminal acts abroad. These restrictions arrive as China and the United States remain locked in a technological arms race, with both nations trading accusations of stealing AI models. While Beijing frames this as a security necessity, analyst Chong Ja Ian warns that terms like security and criminal activities are vaguely defined. This gives the government a wide remit to adjust who is banned from traveling.

Major rail disruptions hit the Netherlands on Tuesday after suspected sabotage to the tracks. Infrastructure operator ProRail reported that pipes were deliberately attached to tracks in multiple locations, causing cancellations and delays across the center and north of the country. The disruption affected routes to Utrecht and Schiphol airport, while Nederlandse Spoorwegen noted that the scale of the incident made bus replacement services impossible. National police are investigating the human action behind these events, though no suspects or motives have been identified. In a separate security concern, enterprises are struggling to manage risks as cloud adoption grows in the age of AI. While some organizations face physical infrastructure attacks, others deal with digital vulnerabilities; Dark Reading reports that most companies were not equipped to contain critical security incidents last year. This gap has led to new initiatives focused on securing multi-cloud environments against evolving cyber threats.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with rain chances up to 75 percent and temperatures between 17 and 24 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your work calendar has a RAYX meeting at three in the afternoon. Your personal calendar has an appointment with Krebs at six in the evening.
Mail worth checking: Steam sent a notice that RimWorld and another item from your wishlist are now on sale.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
